_doc: Regex rules of semantics/tools/trace_requirements.py (basis rule:<id>). Each rule: id, pattern (Python re, case-insensitive, searched in the named fields joined by a space; default field: statement), optional kinds / modules / not_modules filters, targets, why. Patterns are kept specific (word boundaries, scope qualifiers); a missed trace falls to the functional fallback (B, T) or stays open (I, X, P), which is preferred to a wrong trace. Precision is measured in data/trace_sample_review.json. Round 2 (after the round-1 review in data/trace_sample_review.json): read-purity 'reads only' now needs the sentence to end there; 'recorded graph' is no ledger record; redaction verbs need removal context and cost statements are excluded from AX-10; the BM25 version-gate rule needs an upgrade or layout word; AX-04 also matches 'at once or not at all'.

rules.pattern: \b(only|no other|nothing (else|outside))\b[^.]{0,60}\b(class|classes|module|writer|code|path|owner|routine)\b[^.]{0,40}\b(writes?|sets?|kills?|makes?|changes?|touch(es)?)\b|\bno code outside\b|\bgoes through (it|the)\b|\bevery (other )?(caller|writer) goes through\b|\bone writer\b|\bthe one writer\b
rules.why: A store owned by one writer (SYS-I1, ADR-0011, ADR-0002).
States which graph(s) a command reads or changes: an instance of graph scope (SYS-I2 extended).

rules.pattern: \bnames? no graph\b|\ball-graphs\b|\bgraph keys?\b|\buse graph\b|\bper[- ]graph\b|\bacross graphs\b|\bcross(es)? graphs\b|\bmix(es)? graphs\b|\bin (its|their|the edge's|each edge's|that) graph\b|\bgraph by graph\b|\bscoped (query|read|write|lookup)\b
rules.why: Graph-scope vocabulary (CONTEXT.md:27-59).
Tenant separation (SYS-D14, SYS-I2).
A refusal or failure and what it leaves and says (SYS-I3, SYS-I9).

rules.pattern: \b(in|inside|within|as) (one|a single|its own|the same|a new|the caller's|one server) transactions?\b|\bone transaction\b|\ball or nothing\b|\ball-or-nothing\b|\bin full or\b|\ball together\b|\bor none\b|\bleaves? none of\b|\brolls? (it |them |the \w+ )?back\b|\btakes? back\b|\bpartly (written|done)\b|\bhalf[- ]written\b|\ball at once or not at all\b|\bat once or not at all\b
rules.why: Several writes kept together or not at all (SYS-I4).
History only grows; records change only into tombstones (SYS-I5).

rules.pattern: \bretry keys?\b|\bretr(y|ies|ied)\b|\bidempot\w*|\breplay(ed|s)? (commit|answer)\w*|\b(saves?|saved|writes?|written|runs?|ran|applied|applies|creates?|created|commits?|committed|counts?|counted) (it |them |the \w+ )?twice\b|\bsame (retry )?key\b|\b(sends?|sent|resends?|runs?|run) (it |the query |the request )?again\b|\bat most once\b|\bexactly once\b|\bsaves? it once\b|\bgets? (it|the first answer) back\b
rules.why: At most once per retry key or business identity (SYS-I6).

rules.pattern: \b(un)?recorded\b(?! graph)|\bstrict( mode)?\b|\b(ledger|commit)\b[^.]{0,50}\brecords? (it|the|a|each|every|that|them)\b|\bwrites? (a|no|its|the) records?\b|\bwith (its|their) records?\b|\bthe ledger (governs|watches|never sees|sees)\b|\bgoverned\b|\boutside the ledger\b|\bthrough the ledger\b
rules.why: A governed change and its record together; strict mode (SYS-I7).

rules.pattern: \bstale\b|\bout of date\b|\bup to date\b|\brebuil(d|ds|t|ding)\b|\bcached?\b|\bcaches\b|\b(graph-version )?token\b|\bgenerations?\b|\bdrift\b|\b(is|stays?|kept|becomes?|no longer|still) current\b|\bcurrent while\b|\bwarm stamp\b|(?<!-)\bstamp(ed|s)?\b|\bin step\b|\bmatch(es)? (the|its) (rows|text|stored|table)\b|\bagrees? with\b|\bthe two agree\b|\bderived\b|\bkept by\b|\bresync\w*\b
rules.why: A derived store matches its source or says it is stale (SYS-I8, CONTEXT.md:88-128).
One install, one schema, one version; setup idempotent and reporting (SYS-I10).
BM25 index layout version gate (CONTEXT.md:149-153), an instance of the version gate.
Removal of a target's content from every store and copy (erasure, redaction; SYS-D26, SYS-D27).

rules.pattern: \blocks?\b|\blocked\b|\b(two|both|several)\b[^.]{0,60}\bat once\b|\bat the same time\b|\bat a time\b|\bconcurrent\w*\b|\b(two|another|second|other) (writers?|runs?|callers?|workers?|redactions?|builds?|rebuilds?|commits?|erasures?)\b|\bwaits? (for|on)\b|\bwhile (a|another|the|one) (\w+ )?(write|writer|commit|redaction|run|build|sync|rebuild)\w* (runs?|is (running|open|in progress)|holds?|lands?)\b|\bin progress\b|\bopen write\b|\brac(e|es|ing)\b
rules.why: Conflicting commands serialize (locks, markers, waits).
The redaction marker is the exclusive-section signal (ADR-0013).

rules.pattern: \breports?\b|\breported\b|\breceipts?\b|\bsuccess\w*\b|\bhalf done\b|\bpartially\b|\bsays ok\b|\bwarnings?\b|\bdurabl\w*\b|\backnowledg\w*\b|\bonly reads\b|\breads only\b(?=\s*[.,;]|\s+and\b)|\bwrites nothing\b|\bchanges no (data|content)\b|\bcounts? (it|them|what|every|each|the rows|skipped)\b[^.]{0,30}\b(restored|done|removed|written|kept|placed)\b|\bin (its|their) place\b(?=[^.]*\b(answer|empty|result))
rules.why: The reported outcome equals the effect; reads write nothing; observations are committed states.

rules.pattern: \b(api|admin|read) keys?\b|\bread-only\b|\bread only\b|\bprivileges?\b|\b(sql )?rights?\b(?! (end|side))|\broles?\b|\bgrants?\b|\bgranted\b|\blog(s|ged)? in\b|\bpasswords?\b|\bcredentials?\b|\ballow-list\b|\ballowed\b[^.]{0,30}\b(bases|urls?|files?)\b|\bserver files?\b|\blistens? on\b|\bsecurity line\b|\bwho may\b
rules.why: Least capability: keys, roles, read-only, no server-file or code capability.

rules.pattern: \bthe key\b|\bwith a key\b|\bwithout a key\b|\bno key\b|\bwrong key\b|\bkey (check|gate|is set|set)\b|\b401\b|\b403\b
rules.why: The HTTP/Bolt key gate (docs/ADMIN_GUIDE.md section 5).

rules.pattern: \beventually\b|\bresum(e|es|ed|ing)\b|\b(call|called|calls) again\b|\bstarv\w*\b|\bforever\b|\bindefinitely\b|\bnever (finish|finishes|ends|reaches)\b|\bpending\b|\bnext (sync|run|call|resync)\b|\brepeats? it\b|\bstarts? it again\b|\bpicks? up where\b|\bresume point\b
rules.why: Accepted work progresses (no starvation, resumable runs, resources given back).

rules.pattern: \b(process|job|connection) (stops|ends|is stopped|is killed|dies)\b|\bwhen (a|the|its) process (stops|ends)\b|\bstopped (process|run)\b|\bkilled (process|sync|run|writer)\b|\ba killed\b|\bprocess that holds it ends\b
rules.why: Process stop rolls back every level and releases every lock (E-STOP).

rules.pattern: \btransaction levels?\b|\bnew transaction level\b|\bnest(s|ed)? (under|in|inside) the caller's (open )?transaction\b|\bnested level\b|\bits own (transaction )?level\b|\blevels? under (it|them)\b
rules.why: TSTART nests; TROLLBACK 1 undoes the top level only (E-NEST, E-PARTIAL).

rules.pattern: \block (freed|released|unlocked) inside a transaction\b|\bstays held until\b|\bunlock\b[^.]{0,40}\b(commit|transaction ends)\b|\bheld to the end of the transaction\b|\b(frees?|releases?) the (head )?lock\b[^.]{0,40}\bbefore the transaction ends\b
rules.why: An unlock inside a transaction takes effect at the outer end (E-LOCK-DEFER).
Shared locks are compatible, exclusive conflicts (E-LOCK-MODES).
Hierarchical lock names (E-LOCK-NAMES).
Incremental locks of one process (E-LOCK-COUNT).
A waiting lock is granted on release; timeouts (E-LOCK-WAIT).

rules.pattern: \bread[^.]{0,50}\bbefore (it|the writer's transaction|the transaction|its transaction) (commits|ends)\b|\buncommitted\b|\bdirty\b|\bread isolation\b|\bwrite that is still open\b|\bopen write\b|\bother process's open\b
rules.why: No isolation for globals; SQL reads uncommitted rows (E-VIS).

rules.pattern: \bcounter step\b|\badding to a counter\b|\bcount raised in one atomic step\b|\bnot undone by (a )?rollback\b|\brollback does not undo\b|\bnever lowered by a rollback\b|\bsurvives? (a )?rollback\b
rules.why: $Increment is not undone by rollback (E-INCR).
Process-private globals (E-PPG).

rules.pattern: \bwaits? for that transaction\b|\brow another transaction holds\b|\bholds the row\b|\brow locks?\b|\bmeets a row\b
rules.why: Row locks of open transactions (E-ROWLOCK).
Unique keys (E-UNIQUE).

rules.pattern: \btable made inside a transaction\b|\bDDL\b|\b(made|created|dropped) inside a transaction\b|\bdrop table\b
rules.why: DDL and transactions (X-DDL).

rules.pattern: \bempty (string|text)\b[^.]{0,40}\bnull\b|\bnull\b[^.]{0,40}\bempty (string|text|name)\b|\bbinds an empty string\b|\ban empty string as a null\b
rules.why: NULL and the empty string (X-NULL).
Subscript collation and scan order (X-ORDER).
Vector functions available on the engine (X-VEC).

rules.pattern: \bdeclared index\b|\brow hooks?\b|\bfunctional index\b|\binside the row's transaction\b|\beach write of an edge or label row also changes the adjacency index\b
rules.why: Functional index in the row's transaction (X-FX).

rules.pattern: \bfailed (SQL )?statement takes back only its own\b|\bstatement[^.]{0,30}\btakes back only\b
rules.why: Statement atomicity (X-STMT).
SELECT * column order (X-STAR).
%NOINDEX, BUILD INDEX (X-NOINDEX).
SQL and the Native API of one connection share a server process (E-CALLER).
Autocommit (E-AUTOCOMMIT).
Driver commit/rollback levels (E-DRV).
SQL COMMIT/ROLLBACK end one level (E-SQL-END).
SELECT $TLEVEL (X-TLEVEL-SQL).
Routed tables dropped after the erasure's commit (EXC-01).
PurgeAll, outside the growth rule (EXC-02).
Post-commit properties are written after the ledger commit (EXC-03).

rules.pattern: \bvector writes never pass through the ledger\b|\bno revision holds a vector\b|\bvectors?\b[^.]{0,40}\bnot (in|through) the ledger\b|\bnot the ledger, says\b
rules.why: Vectors are not ledgered (EXC-04).
The documented 30 s route memory (EXC-05).

rules.pattern: \binterned snapshot\b[^.]{0,80}\b(no graph|every graph|all graphs|default graph|named graph)\b|\b(no graph|every graph|all graphs|named graph)\b[^.]{0,80}\binterned snapshot\b
rules.why: The interned snapshot has no graph dimension (EXC-06).
A tombstone keeps shape and digest (EXC-07).

rules.pattern: \bnot undone by (a )?rollback\b|\brollback does not undo a counter\b|\bnever lowered by a rollback\b|\bsurvives? (a )?rollback\b|\bthe token never falls\b
rules.why: Monotone counters survive rollback (EXC-08).
Legacy objects stay until removed (EXC-09).
Replay equals the governed store (domain contract, 3.3a-domain-contract).
